key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 perovskites strongly tunes electronic and photovoltaic performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best solar-cell candidate.
engineering_relevance: This suggests composition engineering can optimize perovskite absorbers for higher-efficiency photovoltaic devices without changing the core crystal family.
method: First-principles study of structural, electronic, and optical properties
Band-structure analysis to determine bandgap type and magnitude
SLME-based screening to compare solar-cell efficiency across F, Cl, Br, and I variants
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps from 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME results ranging from 0.6% for Ca3PF3 to 29.6% for Ca3PI3.
watch_item: The reported efficiencies are computational screening results, so experimental stability, defect tolerance, and device-architecture effects still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
